allow_large: The owner asked for this on 2026-10-02 (one explicit workers setting with three values, visible routing); six code files plus the tests and docs the contract change touches

amendments.because: The owner said on 2026-10-02 that Forge keeps no legacy: no one-time rewrite of codex to split
amendments.done_when: forge.toml's workers takes codex (every task and fix on Codex, user-facing included, using the design model's codex entry for user-facing work), claude (everything on Claude) or split (user-facing story tasks on Claude, the rest on Codex: today's behaviour). forge sync changes an existing workers = "codex" to "split" once, so an upgrade keeps behaviour and the file says it; new repos get split written explicitly. forge work prints one line before starting naming the worker, model and effort and why (for example 'Building PERMFLOW-1/T5 with Claude (claude-opus-5-5, high) because it is user-facing (workers = split)'), and forge next shows the worker beside each ready task. If the worker family changes between rounds of one item, the next forge work starts a fresh session on the new worker with the brief and the latest review findings. The skill and the AGENTS.md block explain the three values in one line each. Command-level tests cover each value for a user-facing task and a plain task, the sync rewrite, the printed line, and a family switch between rounds.

findings.body: This change only adds the fix record; the promised behavior remains unimplemented. `src/forge/repo.py:139` accepts only claude and codex, so split is rejected. `src/forge/worker.py:63–66` still overrides codex for user-facing client tasks, and line 125 launches Claude using its design model. `src/forge/init.py:111` still writes codex for new repos. The worker launch paths contain no required pre-start worker/model/effort/reason line, and `src/forge/nextstep.py:335–338` lists ready tasks without their worker. Session selection at `src/forge/worker.py:88–96` and `src/forge/codex.py:175–185` does not check the previous round's worker family, so switching Codex → Claude → Codex can resume the earlier Codex session instead of starting fresh with the full brief. Neither `src/forge/templates/skill.md` nor `src/forge/templates/adapters/AGENTS.md` explains the three values. Implement these requirements before closing this fix; recording them does not resolve the reported routing problem.
findings.title: Not done: forge.toml's workers takes codex, claude or split with explicit routing, visibility and fresh sessions

findings.body: No tests are added or updated for the new contract. Existing command tests enforce the opposite behavior: `tests/test_design_route.py:22–28` expects a user-facing task with codex configured to invoke Claude and make no Codex turn, while `tests/test_fix_new_repos_get_claude_as_their_worker_by.py:24–30` expects new repos to write codex. Add or update real Forge command tests covering all three settings for user-facing and plain tasks, Codex's design-model selection, explicit split initialization, preservation of existing codex configuration, the pre-start explanation, workers beside ready tasks, and a family switch that starts a fresh session carrying the brief and latest findings. These are required acceptance tests owned by this fix; the existing suite cannot demonstrate completion.
findings.title: Not done: command-level tests for worker choices, launch output, ready-task workers and family switches

why: A story task marked user-facing always goes to a Claude worker even when forge.toml says workers = "codex", and nothing in forge.toml, forge next or forge work says so; the owner wants which agent builds what to be visible and switchable in one place
